newsitem.title: USA: Ingersoll-Rand buys more than 85 percent of Newman Tonks.
newsitem.headline: Ingersoll-Rand buys more than 85 percent of Newman Tonks.

text.p: Ingersoll-Rand Co. said Thursday it has acquired more than 85 percent of the shares of Newman Tonks Group Plc, a British producer of architectural hardware.
The acquisition values Newman Tonks at about 230 million pounds ($377 million), Ingersoll-Rand said.
Ingersoll-Rand, which announced its offer to buy Newman Tonks on Jan. 27, said the combination "creates significant growth opportunities for Ingersoll-Rand's architectural hardware business."

Newman Tonks, based in Birmingham, England, makes and supplies branded architectural products for the building industry. Ingersoll-Rand said the company had 1996 sales of about 259 million pounds ($425 million) and about 4,000 employees worldwide.
Ingersoll-Rand, based in Woodcliff Lake, N. J., manufactures and markets air compressors, construction and mining equipment and industrial machinery.
Ingersoll-Rand's stock was down 50 cents at $42 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
